newsitem.title: INDIA: Train blast in northeast India kills seven.
newsitem.headline: Train blast in northeast India kills seven.

text.p: Seven people were killed and eight injured on Thursday when a bomb planted by suspected separatists exploded on a train track in northeastern India, derailing a passenger carriage, police said.
It was the latest attack in a mounting campaign of insurgency-related violence in the region, where dozens of separatist groups are fighting Indian rule.
The army, paramilitary units and police in the region have tightened security ahead of celebrations commemorating India's 50th anniversary of independence due to start on Thursday evening.

A senior police officer told Reuters the Indian government had put security forces, including the army, on full alert in the region after a call by separatist groups for an 18-hour general strike from midnight of August 14.

"For the last one week we are panicky and hope that the 50th year of independence celebration in this part of the country will be peaceful," said a police officer in charge of anti-insurgency operations.
In a statement, six powerful guerrilla groups said that for the people of the region, the 50th anniversary of Independence was the 50th anniversary of their colonial bondage under Indian rule.

In Nagaland bordering Burma, the National Socialist Council of Nagaland warned people against moving about in Kohima and adjacent areas on August 14 and 15 in line with a call to boycott independence day celebrations.
India's northeast, comprising seven hilly states and home to more than 200 ethnic groups, has been racked by separatist violence since India won freedom from British rule.
Authorities said Thursday's blast occurred near Silanibari town in North Lakahimpur district of Assam state, about 200 km (120 miles) east of the region's largest city Guwahati.
Police in Guwahati said 70 to 80 passengers were in the last carriage of the local train when the device went off on the tracks.
Authorities said they had yet to identify who set off the explosion, but they suspected the United Liberation Front of Assam, one of several separatist groups in the state.

In Assam's Kokrajhar district, 15 oil tanks derailed on Wednesday night, police said. Eight tankers, each carrying about 14 tonnes of crude oil, fell on their sides, spilling oil over rice paddy fields.
Police said they suspected sabotage in the incident, which severed rail traffic between the northeast and the rest of India.
On Monday, more than 400 passengers escaped unhurt when tribal guerrillas set off a remote-control bomb on a rail track in Assam.
Tribal guerrillas on Tuesday killed 12 Hindus, executing six after tying them to a tree, in a series of attacks on villages in the state.
Bodo tribal guerrillas on Wednesday attacked an army vehicle, injuring three soldiers, and blew up a bridge in Assam.
Bodo guerrillas have recently stepped up their campaign to have an independent homeland for their tribe's 600,000 members carved out of the oil- and tea-rich state.
Bodo guerrillas have their camps in the foothills of southern Bhutan and accuse Bengali-speaking Hindu immigrants of encroaching on their homeland in Assam.
In neighbouring Manipur state, soldiers killed five tribal guerrillas on Wednesday near the border with Burma.
